title: AI Is Good for for Production, Bad for Learning
author: Chad Aldeman
summary: Chad Aldeman reflects personally on his own growing reliance on AI, noting a split between its production benefits and its cost to his own learning and retention. He credits AI with genuine productivity gains — organizing data, copy editing, generating title ideas, and scraping data that would otherwise have taken days or been abandoned as impossible — including within his own literacy project, Read Not Guess, where AI helps generate audio files and thematic images. But he pairs this admission with a caution: the more he offloads thinking to AI, the less he retains himself, echoing his overarching thesis that AI accelerates output while potentially degrading the learning process behind that output. The piece functions as a first-person case study in the tension between AI-driven efficiency and cognitive engagement, relevant to how educators think about AI use for both themselves and students.
points: Opens with a personal admission: AI helps Aldeman produce more, but he retains less when he lets it think for him.
Credits AI with real production gains — data organizing, copy editing, title generation, and scraping data manually infeasible.
Cites his own project, Read Not Guess, where AI helps generate audio files and thematic pictures.
Draws a clear distinction between AI's usefulness for production tasks versus its risk to genuine learning/retention.
Uses first-person reflection to make a broader point about AI's tradeoffs for anyone doing intellectual work, including students.
quotes: I find myself using AI more and more often. It has helped me to both more stuff and more different kinds of things than I would have been able to do otherwise.
the more I let AI do my thinking for me, the less I seem to retain myself
In my work life, AI can be a great data organizer and copy editor.
I had it scrape a website for data that would have taken me days to capture by hand—in the olden days, I probably would have decided it was impossible and given up.
For Read Not Guess, AI is built into the app version and allows me to quickly create audio files and thematic pictures.
